hero.title: The forfeit wheel to spin as a couple
hero.description: 70 forfeits across seven families. You press, the wheel spins, and it decides instead of you.

familles.bisouDesc: Short, affectionate forfeits, from a kiss on the shoulder to an eskimo kiss. The ones that work anywhere, even in company.
familles.massageDesc: Shoulders, hands, neck, feet: two timed minutes that drop the pressure in one go.
familles.showDesc: Sing, dance, impersonate, declaim. The family that is awkward for five seconds and funny for ten minutes.
familles.aveuDesc: A question you have to answer properly. This is the family that turns a games night into a real conversation.
familles.grimaceDesc: Owning the ridiculous: an imposed accent, an animal to impersonate, a piece of clothing inside out for three spins.
familles.photoDesc: Forfeits that leave a trace, from the ugliest possible selfie to a year-old photo you have to recreate exactly.
familles.douceurDesc: Compliments, written notes, a hug that does not let go. The simplest ones, and often the ones you remember.

section1.title: A forfeit drawn at random beats a forfeit someone invented
section1.p1: When a bet ends, someone has to come up with the forfeit. And that is where it falls apart: either nobody has an idea, or the idea is too harsh, or the winner feels obliged to go easy. In all three cases the moment dies.
section1.p2: A wheel settles it instantly: nobody chose, so nobody is responsible. That is also what makes it possible to accept a forfeit you would have refused had your partner suggested it, because there is no intention behind it any more, only chance.
section1.p3: Seven families sit on the wheel, plus a surprise slot that draws from all the others. You spin as many times as you want: the game has no ending, it stops when you close the page.

section2.title: What is on the wheel
section2.intro: Each family holds its own ten forfeits, written for a couple and playable in a living room. Nothing repeats until the family runs out.

section3.title: How to use it
section3.intro: There is no rulebook imposed on you: the wheel is a tool, you decide what sets it off.
section3.regle1Texte: The most common use. Whoever loses spins the wheel and does what it lands on, without arguing. It works precisely because they did not choose it.
section3.regle2Titre: At the end of another game
section3.regle2Texte: A spin at the end of a quiz or a truth or dare relaunches the evening without having to get another game out.
section3.regle3Titre: As a game in its own right
section3.regle3Texte: Take turns: each of you spins and does what comes up. Ten spins make a full session, and you will not get the same one twice.
section3.regle4Titre: With the right to spin again
section3.regle4Texte: Agree on one thing before you start: either of you can spin again once per evening without justifying it. That removes the only reason not to play.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: 70, split into seven families of ten. The surprise slot draws from all seven, so it adds no forfeits but it changes the way they land.
faq.a2: Not until the family you landed on runs out. Each family reshuffles once its ten forfeits have come up, which is plenty for an evening without hitting the same one.
faq.a3: No, this wheel is built to be spun anywhere, friends included. The most intimate it gets is a kiss or a massage. For something more direct, our truth or dare games have their own separate deck.
faq.q4: Can more than two people play?
faq.a4: The forfeits are written for a couple, but nothing stops you passing the phone around a group: half of them work as they are, the other half simply assume there is a partner opposite you.
faq.a5: No, and nothing is recorded. The wheel runs in your browser, on a phone or a computer, and the counter goes back to zero as soon as you reload the page.

section4.title: A well-chosen forfeit makes nobody uncomfortable
section4.p1: The only real risk with a forfeit game is the forfeit that goes too far for one of you. The ones on this wheel are deliberately living-room sized: nothing that asks anyone to undress, nothing that exposes you in front of others, nothing you would regret the next day.
section4.p2: The rest is yours to decide, and it is far better that way.
